A change of a racket at courtside during a rally is permitted (Instructions to Technical Officials 7.0 (5), in force 2025-04-26, Clause 5.10.1(2)). So when your string breaks during a rally, you are allowed to change your racket at courtside while the rally continues.

Those intervals are: not exceeding 60 seconds during each game when the leading score reaches 11 points, except Handicap matches (Law 16.2.1(1)), and not exceeding 120 seconds between the first and second game and between the second and third game (Law 16.2.2(1)).
Any racket you change to must still be a legal racket under Law 4 of the Laws of Badminton 5.0 (2), in force 2025-04-26: the stringed area shall be flat and consist of crossed strings alternately interlaced or bonded where they cross (Law 4.2.1(1)) and shall not exceed 280 mm in overall length and 220 mm in overall width (Law 4.2.2(1)); the racket shall be free of attached objects and protrusions other than those solely and specifically for wear/tear, vibration, weight distribution or securing the handle, reasonable in size and placement (Law 4.3.1(1)), and free of any device that makes it possible to change materially the shape of the racket (Law 4.3.2(1)).
